# Extensions and marketplace apps

## Scope

Applies when the change touches a browser or editor extension, or an app a host's marketplace lists. Not when a service only calls a host's API and no marketplace lists it, which `aidd-team:apis-and-services` covers. Neighbours: `aidd-team:secure-coding`, `aidd-team:privacy-by-default`, `aidd-team:release-rollout`.

## Dated obligations

| From | Obligation | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2025-11-03 | Every new Firefox extension declares its data collection in `data_collection_permissions`. | S2 |
| 2026-08-31 | The Chrome Web Store removed every remaining Manifest V2 extension: publish and update in Manifest V3 only. | S1 |
| 2026-12-01 | Azure DevOps retires global PATs: VS Code Marketplace publishing moves to Microsoft Entra ID. | S3 |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Name the hosts the change ships to. A new permission, scope, or data use is major, since the host re-reviews it and can reject or delist. | S1, S4, S5 |
| Specify | Each permission, host permission, and OAuth scope with the feature that needs it, the narrowest that works; optional permissions for what only some users need. | S1, S2, S4, S6 |
| Specify | The listing's privacy, terms, and support links. Its AI use: host data never trains a model, and AI output stays within the host's content policy. | S5, S7 |
| Implement | All executable code ships in the package: no remote script, no `eval` of fetched text, no obfuscation (minified is fine). Firefox gets the source and build steps. | S1, S2 |
| Implement | Host rules in code. Shopify: session tokens and Billing API. Atlassian: TLS 1.2+ and HSTS, secrets out of source and logs. VS Code: publishing by Entra ID, never a PAT. | S4, S6, S3 |
| Review | The permission and scope diff, each addition justified in the Spec; for Salesforce, the Code Analyzer and Checkmarx reports clean or false positives documented. | S1, S8 |
| Ship | Submit with a reviewer test account valid while the listing is live, a current screencast, and step-by-step test notes; keep the previous version publishable. | S4, S7, S8 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Permission and scope diff | no permission or OAuth scope was added without a Spec line | diff the extension manifest's permissions, `shopify.app.toml` scopes, the Slack, Forge, or Teams manifest scopes against the last release tag | S1, S2, S4, S5, S6 |
| Remote code scan | the built package runs no remote code and is not obfuscated | `npx web-ext@10.7.0 lint` on the Firefox build; a scan of the built zip for `eval(`, `new Function`, and remote `<script src>` | S1, S2 |
| VSIX contents check | the extension package holds no secret or stray file | `npx @vscode/vsce@4.0.0 package` (fails on a detected secret; no `--allow-package-all-secrets`), then `vsce ls` against an allow-list | S3 |
| Listing links without sign-in | the privacy, terms, and support pages load for a signed-out visitor | `curl -fsSL` each listing URL with no cookie, in CI | S5, S7 |
| Reviewer access check | the reviewer test account signs in and reaches every listed feature | a scheduled smoke test with the submission's test account | S4, S7, S8 |
| Host billing test | every charge goes through the host's billing API and survives a reinstall | on a Shopify development store, a test charge approved, declined, and re-requested after reinstall | S4 |
| AI data-use check | no host-sourced data reaches a training job, and the listing states the AI use | a test over the training pipeline's inputs, tagged by source; a text check of the listing | S5, S7 |
| Salesforce Code Analyzer scan | the managed package passes the review's scanner | `sf code-analyzer run --rule-selector AppExchange --rule-selector Recommended:Security --output-file CodeAnalyzerReport.html` | S8 |

## References

- [references/hosts.md](references/hosts.md): each host's review rules, reviewer access, billing, AI rules, and publishing credentials, each with its source and date. The hosts: Chrome, Firefox, VS Code, Shopify, Slack, Atlassian, Teams, and Salesforce.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/roles.json`.
